value: This humorous song, styled after Gilbert and Sullivan, presents a self-portrait of an Informatics Lecturer. The lecturer boasts extensive knowledge in theoretical computer science, covering topics like formal languages, parsing algorithms, programming language theory, mathematical logic, set theory, and the philosophy of mathematics. However, the persona humorously admits a significant lack of practical modern computing skills, from networking to contemporary web development, confessing their expertise largely predates the 20th century. Despite this humorous gap in practical "IT skills," the song playfully asserts that foundational knowledge, combined with an engaging teaching style, remains paramount in shaping an "Informatics lecturer" model.
